corrected_value.title: Environmental disorder leads to self-regulatory failure.

decisions.quote: All Order-Disorder comparisons were not significant also in the case of the executive functioning measures (see Table 1 ). Results remained unchanged after removing outliers scores 3 SD away from the mean ( n = 5). Ancillary Analysis A series of additional analyses were conducted to test differences between task rotations. We also compared the effect of experimental conditions only considering the rotations that most closely resembled the task order in Vohs et al. (2013) and Chae and Zhu (2014) .
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent. In addition to testing Vohs et al.'s (2013) disorder-creativity effect (shipped row 2478), this paper tests whether workspace disorder impairs executive functioning as reported by Chae and Zhu (2014). In Results (Table 1 and Ancillary Analysis), the authors compare Order vs. Disorder conditions on multiple executive control measures, including task-order rotations aligned specifically with Chae and Zhu (2014), and in Discussion they directly contrast their null executive-functioning results and larger sample size (n = 50 per group vs. 20-25) with Chae and Zhu (2014). The reference list (lines 5-6) confirms the identity (Journal of Consumer Research, 40, 1203-1218, doi:10.1086/674547), which is an independent study from shipped row 2478 (Vohs et al., 2013).
